![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14230052/assets/994b8cd2134d6d1e9a1e89559e462128c05fd5d3e7f4755c51931f3cf7f37268.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the path along the polar curve $r={\theta }^{2}\,$ for $0\le \theta \le \pi ,$ shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to arc length over $C$ is equal to the arc length $L$ of $C,$ i.e.,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.
$$

In polar coordinates, the arc length element $\text{d}s$ is given by

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

So, for a polar curve defined as $r=r(\theta )$ for ${\theta }_{1}\le \theta \le {\theta }_{2},$ we have

$$
L={\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r={\theta }^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=2\theta .
$$

Therefore, we evaluate our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{({\theta }^{2})}^{2}+{(2\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{\theta }^{4}+4{\theta }^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{\theta }^{2}(4+{\theta }^{2})}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\theta \sqrt{4+{\theta }^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\theta \sqrt{4+{\theta }^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\frac{{(4+{\theta }^{2})}^{3/2}}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{{({\pi }^{2}+4)}^{3/2}-8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
